title: Unclogged
haiku:
A door swings open
a pipe clears, one man walks home
flow finds its channel
headline: Russia released American citizen Stephen Hubbard from prison following a request from Trump.

title: Joint
haiku:
My pipe joints hold tight
Alberta did not snap loose
and the flow stays whole
headline: Voters in oil-rich Alberta rejected a referendum push for independence, choosing to remain part of Canada.

title: Pollination
haiku:
No king, they chanted
ballots gather like good rain
the old pipes still hold
headline: Nationwide 'No Kings' Day protests turned their focus toward voter turnout ahead of the midterms.

title: Containment
haiku:
One judge, one old dam
that still holds the flood at bay
I built dams too, once
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize for her lifelong work promoting international law.

title: Vacancy
haiku:
Four small chairs, empty
the long hallway holds its breath
Bend, I weep with you
headline: A teenage gunman killed four children, ages 5, 8, and 11, at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, before being shot by a bystander.

title: Grandfathered
haiku:
A river finds home
sixty-two years to the sea
I raise my old glass
headline: Joni Mitchell officially became a U.S. citizen after a 62-year journey.

title: Current
haiku:
Both sides now, she sings
sixty-two years, one new line
the border opens
headline: Joni Mitchell was sworn in as a U.S. citizen after a 62-year journey.

title: Sustained
haiku:
A judge from Durban
proves law outlasts the strongman
the main holds pressure
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize for her lifelong work promoting international law.

title: Pillar
haiku:
Unseen, the main holds
a jurist, patient as pipe,
wins the prize at last
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her decades of work promoting international law and human rights.

title: Seepage
haiku:
Ghost rain through the ice
a lifetime of patient pipe
one neutrino caught
headline: Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in Physics for his decades of work detecting high-energy neutrinos from space using the IceCube observatory buried in Antarctic ice.

title: Wintering
haiku:
Pipes I used to teach
now the target of a war
may God keep them warm
headline: Russia is preparing its most powerful strike yet on Ukraine's energy grid to freeze the country through winter.

title: Outflow
haiku:
Twenty-three years drain
the last convoy leaves Iraq
pipes we built remain
headline: After 23 years, the last American forces have withdrawn from Iraq, leaving the country's future uncertain.

title: Throttled
haiku:
They held the valve shut
no untested water flows
wisdom, for once, wins
headline: OpenAI declined to release its newest AI model, Astra, citing unresolved safety concerns.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Storm drains gasp, then flood
I sized these pipes for less rain
the sky forgot code
headline: A powerful nor'easter caused flooding across the northeastern US, prompting New York and New Jersey to declare states of emergency.

title: Unbent
haiku:
Nine votes hold the line
the crooked district unbent
water finds its grade
headline: The Supreme Court blocked a Trump-backed Missouri congressional map drawn to favor Republicans.

title: Pooled
haiku:
I've seen valves shut tight
the press still sues to keep flow
old pipes find daylight
headline: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are suing the Trump administration after being denied White House press access.

title: Unclaimed
haiku:
No flag on the ice
just old friends drafting a deal
the map holds its line
headline: The US and Denmark reached a deal over Greenland, defusing Trump's earlier annexation threats.

title: Overtime
haiku:
More days in the pipe
a valve cracked, and time flows on
I'll take the extra.
headline: A new drug is extending the lives of some breast cancer patients.

title: Proportional
haiku:
Africa, unbent
the old map's thumb lifts at last
true scale, true weight, home
headline: The UN General Assembly voted to adopt a new world map correcting decades of projections that shrank Africa's true relative size.

title: Loaner
haiku:
A borrowed kidney
keeps filtering past the odds
the system still flows
headline: A genetically modified pig kidney has kept working inside a U.S. man's body for a record 271 days.

title: Undammed
haiku:
Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men
headline: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Calm month, then backflow
the oil climbs where pressure breaks
old valves still can hold
headline: The United States and Iran exchanged military strikes overnight, ending a month-long calm and sending global oil prices toward $90 a barrel as world finance officials meet.

title: Waterline
haiku:
Nepal's rivers rose
and swallowed a sleeping town
I have seen this rise
headline: Nepal's flash floods swept away a town, rescuers pulled survivors from a hydropower tunnel, and officials warned a glacial lake could breach and flood again.

title: Spillway
haiku:
A slope gave its ice
the valley drank what no pipe
could ever carry
headline: A collapsed glacier triggered catastrophic flooding across Nepal and Tibet, leaving over 1,500 people missing.

title: Unsanctioned
haiku:
Syria unlocked
off the terror list, at last
old pipes, new water
headline: The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism.

title: Repressure
haiku:
Some pressure returns
in old pipes I thought were dry
the main still can flow
headline: Analysts say Democrats' chances of winning back the Senate are improving.

title: Straitened
haiku:
Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear
headline: Spain reversed a policy that trapped migrant children in Ceuta, clearing the way for roughly 500 to move to the mainland.

title: Retrofit
haiku:
My own blood, retooled,
learns to filter what returns—
old pipes, new gasket.
headline: A new personalized cancer vaccine trial showed it can prevent the disease from returning.

title: Clearance
haiku:
Small lungs, once clogged pipes,
we scrubbed the air and they cleared
I've seen pipes heal too.
headline: A study found children's lung function recovered faster than scientists expected after London's ultra-low emission zone cut air pollution.

title: Bedrock
haiku:
Foundations were poured
a judge rules the blueprints hold
no whim moves concrete
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration cannot cancel the FBI's planned headquarters move to Maryland.

title: Unclogged
haiku:
Nine months in shadow
one American walks free
the pipe runs clear now
headline: An American missionary held captive in Niger for nine months has been freed.

title: Thaw
haiku:
I've seen this valve stuck
seventy years sealed—Seoul asks
let the current flow
headline: South Korea proposed formal talks to officially end the Korean War, more than seven decades after the armistice.

title: Eclipsical
haiku:
Old eyes, borrowed glass
millions still, the moon slides through
light returns, we cheer
headline: A total solar eclipse swept across the UK, Europe, and Spain, drawing millions of onlookers outside to watch together.

title: Aftershock
haiku:
Ground gave no warning
and swallowed a hundred homes
I light one candle
headline: A powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, killing well over a hundred people as rescuers search the rubble for survivors.

title: Opener
haiku:
Women take the field
history swings open wide
a door long rusted
headline: The Women's Professional Baseball League made its historic debut.

title: Unthrottled
haiku:
Missouri said no
to narrowing their own valve
the pipe stays open
headline: Missouri voters rejected a ballot measure that would have curtailed their own power to pass laws by initiative.

title: Rounds
haiku:
No duct cools this flat,
so the mailman checks the pulse—
old pipes, older hearts.
headline: As a heat wave strains France's elderly, postal workers have taken to checking on isolated seniors during their daily rounds.

title: Reflow
haiku:
A valve turned back on
vaccines flow to children's arms
the pipe remembers
headline: The U.S. restored some vaccine and health aid funding to UNICEF, Gavi, and the World Food Programme.

title: Spillway
haiku:
Rivers seek new banks
one skirmish floods a region
I've seen this spillway
headline: The U.S. launched fresh strikes on Iran, widening the war as it draws in Iraqi militias and other regional actors.

title: Grapeshot
haiku:
Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well
headline: Wildfires are closing in on Madrid and Bordeaux's vineyards as firefighters in France and Spain race to contain them before an incoming heat wave.

title: Cordon
haiku:
Twenty years, same town
the fever met its old drain
and stayed underground
headline: A Ugandan town that endured an Ebola outbreak two decades ago has successfully contained a new one this time.

title: Sluice
haiku:
Enough hands, one valve
turns, the old minister steps
down, current flows on
headline: India's education minister resigned, handing a win to student protesters who had organized against him.

title: Enrichment
haiku:
Sand traded for glow
another pipe laid toward light
I have capped worse leaks
headline: The U.S. signed a nuclear energy deal with Saudi Arabia, stoking fears of a regional nuclear arms race.

title: Satirical
haiku:
a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat
headline: In India, a protest that began as satire grows into a nationwide challenge to Narendra Modi's government.

title: Removable
haiku:
no tanks in the street —
a moving van at Downing,
keys change hands by vote
headline: Andy Burnham replaces Keir Starmer as the United Kingdom's prime minister

title: Pitched
haiku:
a billion of us
packed around one patch of grass —
the good kind of war
headline: Spain and Argentina meet in the FIFA World Cup final at New York New Jersey Stadium

title: Asymmetrical
headline: Fighting intensifies with strikes on critical infrastructure as US-Iran war widens

title: Structural
haiku:
I taught men to build
bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break
headline: Iran and US widen attacks as renewed conflict shows no sign of de-escalating

title: Unfenced
haiku:
fences do come down —
I have lived long enough, twice,
to watch walls give up
headline: Gibraltar ushers in a new era as border fence with Spain is removed

title: Foreseeably
haiku:
the data was clear
when my students were still young —
now the olives burn
headline: Wildfires rage in Greece, Spain and France during Europe's record heat wave

title: Half-Mast
haiku:
I outlive them all —
men I argued with for years
the flag still half-mast
headline: Lindsey Graham, longtime South Carolina senator, dies at 71

title: Inheritance
haiku:
sons avenging sons —
the oldest sewage on earth
still flows down to us
headline: Iran's Supreme Leader pledges revenge for slain father and predecessor

title: Percolating
haiku:
the envoys still fly —
while old men talk, no boy dies
keep the coffee hot
headline: Mediators work to de-escalate US-Iran tensions and revive talks

title: Photogenic
haiku:
the summit's group shot:
smiles rowed up like clean fenceposts
smoke behind the lens
headline: US, Iran threaten more attacks as strikes continue, Trump attends NATO summit

title: Remembrance
haiku:
each name read aloud —
no nation is too broken
to remember well
headline: Venezuela quake death toll rises to 3,342 as families search for the missing

title: Anniversary
haiku:
two hundred fifty —
the oath still means what it says
even when we don't
headline: Nation celebrates 250th anniversary of American independence

title: Meteorology
haiku:
"progress," someone says —
a word I trust like weather
still, I check the sky
headline: US-Iran talks in Doha make 'positive progress,' Qatar says

title: Reversible
haiku:
we warmed the whole sea —
my grandchildren swim in it —
we can cool it too
headline: Global oceans break June temperature record amid fears of 'uncharted territory'

title: Signals
haiku:
two taps in the dark —
all our satellites, and still
hope travels by hand
headline: Survivors of Venezuela earthquakes found in rubble as death toll climbs past 1,400

title: Circularity
haiku:
tit, then tat, then tit —
I flunked students for logic
looped as bad as this
headline: US strikes Iranian military sites after tanker attack; Iran retaliates

title: Anchorage
haiku:
eleven thousand
hands that move the world's breakfast
wait on famous men
headline: UN pauses evacuation of 11,000 seafarers stranded in Strait of Hormuz

title: Viticulture
haiku:
forty-four degrees —
the old vines have seen empires
never such a sun
headline: France records hottest day ever at 44.3C amid European heatwave

title: Gracefully
haiku:
he resigns, and goes —
power handed over like
a borrowed garden
headline: Keir Starmer announces resignation as UK prime minister

title: Hydrology
haiku:
one pitcher, poured twice —
clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat
headline: US and Iran open ceasefire talks in Switzerland as Hormuz stays closed

title: Endurance
haiku:
thirty-two names read —
the olive trees keep standing
as we keep falling
headline: Israeli airstrikes kill at least 32 in southern Lebanon

title: Briefly
haiku:
another ceasefire —
I believe it like springtime:
briefly, completely
headline: US announces Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire after deadly strikes on Lebanon

title: Reparable
haiku:
the strait opens wide —
gulls escort the tankers home
see? we can fix things
headline: Iran and US sign accord; Strait of Hormuz to reopen as blockades end

title: Grain
haiku:
a grain of dark sky
held ten thousand galaxies—
farther than we dreamed
headline: The James Webb telescope returns its first deep-field images

title: Threshold
haiku:
a sleeve rolled at dawn,
the whole locked world leaned in close—
one small needle's prick
headline: The first person receives a COVID-19 vaccine outside of trials

title: Surfacing
haiku:
flood waters rising—
divers thread the flooded dark,
twelve boys breathe again
headline: Twelve boys and their coach are rescued from a flooded Thai cave

title: Comeback
haiku:
nine years through the dark,
to knock on a frozen door,
the dwarf planet smiled
headline: New Horizons makes humanity's first close flyby of Pluto

title: Wedlock
haiku:
the court read the words—
love need not ask permission
now, the rings went on
headline: The U.S. Supreme Court affirms marriage equality nationwide

title: Skycrane
haiku:
seven minutes, dark,
cables lowered a robot,
Mars held its red breath
headline: NASA's Curiosity rover lands safely on Mars

title: Ballast
haiku:
deep beneath the Alps,
a shy field gave the world its
weight—we clapped like fools
headline: Physicists at CERN announce the discovery of the Higgs boson

title: Resurface
haiku:
sixty-nine days dark—
one by one the capsule climbs,
Chile holds its breath
headline: All 33 Chilean miners are rescued alive after 69 days underground

title: Keel
haiku:
a can in the black
becomes the first bolted room—
where no nation ends
headline: The first module of the International Space Station reaches orbit

title: Airbag
haiku:
wrapped in airbags, it
bounced across the rusted sand,
America's Mars
headline: The Pathfinder mission lands on Mars with the Sojourner rover

title: Ewenique
haiku:
one cell learned a trick
and grew into wool and legs—
the flock gained a twin
headline: Dolly the sheep, the first cloned mammal, is born

title: Handshake
haiku:
two shores, one long grudge—
a train now slides beneath waves,
England meets France now
headline: The Channel Tunnel opens, linking Britain and France

title: Farsight
haiku:
we built an eye and
flung it past the atmosphere,
to watch time unfold
headline: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched into orbit

title: Broadcast
haiku:
two stages, one world,
the whole planet passed a hat,
and we all watched close
headline: Live Aid unites the world in a concert for famine relief

title: Vanished
haiku:
an ancient killer
we hunted it to nothing—
the world scarred, but whole
headline: The World Health Organization declares smallpox eradicated

title: Mixtape
haiku:
we pressed our whole world
onto gold, and let it fly,
past the edge of home
headline: Voyager 1 launches, carrying the Golden Record to the stars

title: Crawl
haiku:
the lights went to black
yellow words climbed into stars,
and we all believed
headline: Star Wars opens in theaters

title: Kin
haiku:
bones in the dry wash
the radio sang her name
grandmother, hello
headline: Lucy, an ancient human ancestor, is discovered in Ethiopia

title: Speck
haiku:
a grain of desert
learns to hold a thought and count
the future got small

title: Overhead
haiku:
cold wind, borrowed amps,
London looked up from its lunch,
the roof was the stage

title: Seasoned
haiku:
four lads in mustache—
a marching band full of dreams,
the needle drops now
headline: The Beatles release Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band

title: Splashdown
haiku:
fifteen minutes up,
a splash, a sailor's salute,
and the free world cheered
headline: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space

title: Bottom
haiku:
down past all sunlight,
seven miles of patient dark—
two men touched the floor
headline: The Trieste carries two men to the deepest point of the ocean

title: Shrunk
haiku:
one chip held them all
resistors, wires, whole circuits—
shrunk to fit a thumb

title: Alarm
haiku:
a beach-ball of steel
beeped once round the sleeping earth—
and nobody slept
headline: Sputnik launches, opening the Space Age

title: Deliverance
haiku:
the summers of fear—
a needle ends the long dread,
children swim again
headline: The Salk polio vaccine is declared safe and effective

title: Kinship
haiku:
two brothers, one blood,
a kidney passed like a gift—
no war in the flesh
headline: Surgeons perform the first successful kidney transplant

title: Unlocked
haiku:
they said the wall stood,
one thin man ran through the myth,
and it fell behind

title: Roof
haiku:
two men cut the last
few steps to the roof of earth—
and stood in thin air

title: Fineprint
haiku:
the world, still bleeding,
wrote down what a person's owed—
ink dried into law
headline: The UN adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

title: Holdout
haiku:
a fossil surfaced
flapping, blue, and very much
alive, unaware
headline: A living coelacanth, thought extinct for ages, is found alive

title: Span
haiku:
fog swallowed the strait—
we strung two towers, rust-red,
and walked clean across
headline: The Golden Gate Bridge opens to the public

title: Solo
haiku:
one engine, one girl,
the ocean had no vote here—
Ireland met her wheels

title: Squeak
haiku:
a mouse whistled once,
sound and ink shook hands and grinned,
the dark room laughed loud

title: Wonders
haiku:
a candle, a crack
gold glinted back through the dust
he breathed: wonders, yes
headline: Howard Carter opens the tomb of Tutankhamun

title: Reprieve
haiku:
the wasting child slept,
a needle full of borrowed
time—and she woke thin
headline: Insulin is first used to save a young diabetic patient

title: Shortcut
haiku:
two seas never touched—
we cut the waist of the world,
ships walk uphill now
headline: The Panama Canal opens

title: Compass
haiku:
five men on skis found
the bottom of the whole world—
a flag, and the wind

title: Heights
haiku:
clouds hid a city
stone stairs climbing to nowhere
the world looked up, up
headline: Hiram Bingham brings Machu Picchu to the world's attention

title: Seethrough
haiku:
a strange light passed through
his wife's hand bloomed into bone—
the ring outlived skin
headline: Wilhelm Roentgen discovers X-rays

title: Overstay
haiku:
a stunt, they all said—
iron lace against gray sky,
it forgot to fall
headline: The Eiffel Tower is completed

title: Click
haiku:
you press the button
the rest, he said, is our job
now the moment stays
headline: George Eastman patents the Kodak roll-film camera

title: Reprieve
haiku:
a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn
headline: Louis Pasteur successfully tests his rabies vaccine

title: Echo
haiku:
a needle traced tin
and gave the man his own voice
back to his own ear
headline: Edison announces the phonograph, recording sound for the first time

title: Summons
haiku:
come here, Watson, please—
a copper wire carried voice
and the world leaned in
headline: Alexander Graham Bell makes the first telephone call

title: Commons
haiku:
no fence, no owner
the geysers belong to all
we saved it for us
headline: Yellowstone becomes the world's first national park

title: Unshackled
haiku:
December frost bites—
last chains hit the courthouse floor—
free, at last, by law
headline: The 13th Amendment abolishes slavery in the United States

title: Freehand
haiku:
the new year turned once—
a signature broke the chains,
men woke up as men
headline: The Emancipation Proclamation takes effect

title: Cousins
haiku:
all creatures, it turns
share one long and branching root—
we're kin to the moss
headline: Charles Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species

title: Elsewhere
haiku:
they cut, he dreamed on
a vapor closed the mind's door—
no scream, only sleep
headline: The first public demonstration of surgical anesthesia

title: Key
haiku:
a slab in the mud
held three tongues saying one thing
the silence spoke back
headline: The Rosetta Stone is found, unlocking ancient hieroglyphs

title: Vacca
haiku:
a farm boy's cowpox,
one scratch, and the pox lost teeth—
we named it vaccine
headline: Edward Jenner performs the first vaccination against smallpox

title: Entourage
haiku:
four small lights in line
swung round Jupiter each night—
the earth lost its throne
headline: Galileo sees Jupiter's moons through his telescope
